messages:
kevin: Quick question — for the internal model-serving APIs do we want a thin HTTP JSON passthrough, or build a small transport adapter that speaks both gRPC and JSON? Thinking about client ergonomics vs operational surface.

maria: my vote: adapter. We keep a stable business contract (protobuf) and translate for web/legacy clients. avoids duplicating logic. :+1:

sanjay: adapter is good but surface area increases. who owns proto->json mapping? camelCase vs snake_case, enums, edge cases (bytes)?

olivia: Agree with sanjay. Also worried about telemetry and quotas. If adapter rewrites requests we must preserve original trace/span ids and per-tenant headers. Otherwise billing/alerts get wrong.

kevin: good point. proposal: adapter in front of runtime that does: 1) content-type routing (application/grpc vs application/json), 2) header passthrough with whitelist, 3) lightweight validations, 4) emit unified telemetry tags.

maria: that seems sane. can we make the adapter stateless and deploy as sidecar or as a small edge pool? Sidecar gives lowest latency for dedicated flows. Edge pool easier to roll out. tradeoffs?

sanjay: sidecar -> simpler routing + per-pod quotas. edge pool -> central control, easier to autoscale, but introduces another network hop and single point for rate-limiting rules.

olivia: for rollout UX, we should support config-driven mapping so we can A/B the adapter on a subset of traffic. Example YAML config idea:

```yaml
routes:
  - match: {path: /v1/generate, content_type: application/json}
    backend: runtime-grpc
    transform: json_to_proto
    headers_preserve: [x-request-id, x-tenant-id, x-traceparent]
    telemetry_tags: [route, tenant, client_version]
```

maria: nice. also add a flag to preserve original payload when transform fails and return a 400 + structured error so clients can auto-retry with corrected shape.

kevin: implementation note: Go + yqlib for transformation? or use generated proto JSON (google.golang.org/protobuf) to avoid edge cases with bytes/base64?

sanjay: use generated proto JSON; safer for enums/bytes. but we'll need a small shim to accept `content-type: application/x-ndjson` too for streaming uses.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for adapter v0.1 on cluster: inference-edge (target 5% traffic).

olivia: re telemetry — ensure the adapter tags the span with `adapter.variant` so we can detect regressions in latency or output quality quickly. also tie into existing dashboards: per-route P50/P95, error-rate, and token-cost estimates.

kevin: agree. action items: @maria prototype adapter config + simple json->proto transform (due EOD Fri), @sanjay add proto JSON roundtrip tests + streaming ndjson example, @olivia add telemetry panel stubs for canary. i'll coordinate rollout plan and ownership.

maria: on it. will start with a minimal path that only handles /v1/generate and rejects unknown fields.

kevin: sweet. thanks all. we'll sync async updates in this thread. :rocket:
